scenes.heading: Choosing your VA specialty and ideal client type

sents.d: Choosing your VA specialty and ideal client type
A defined specialty makes marketing and pricing much easier than generalist positioning.

'Virtual assistant' covers an enormous range of work — inbox and calendar management, customer support, bookkeeping support, social media scheduling, project coordination — and trying to offer all of it makes it hard for potential clients to know if you're the right fit.

Choosing a specialty based on skills you already have or genuinely enjoy (rather than whichever seems most in-demand) tends to produce better client relationships and more sustainable motivation over time.
Pairing a service specialty with an ideal client type (e.g. 'inbox and calendar management for solo consultants') gives you a much more specific and referable position than general availability.

take: Specialize in one service for one type of client.
